newsitem.title: USA: Unisys profits boosted by growth in all businesses.
newsitem.headline: Unisys profits boosted by growth in all businesses.

text.p: Unisys Corp. Monday reported strong first-quarter results, boosted by growth in its computer systems, global customer services and information services businesses.

Unisys earned $19.3 million, or 6 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 31, compared with a net loss of $13.4 million, or 25 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenue rose 8 percent to $1.53 billion from $1.42 billion despite the negative impact of the strong dollar.

"Driven by strong results from our Computer Systems business and another solid performance from our Global Customer Services unit, the company grew its revenue while significantly improving its profitability and operating cash flow from a year ago," said James Unruh, chairman and CEO.

"After delivering quarter-to-quarter improvement in 1996, we continue to clearly build momentum under our three-business, one-company structure. We are on track toward our goals of delivering quarterly, year-over-year financial progress and full-year profitability in 1997."

Revenue and profit gains in the Computer Systems Group were driven by strong demand for Unisys' ClearPath enterprise server systems. The performance of Global Customer Services was driven by continued strong growth in distributed computing support services.

Unisys said its Information Services Group continued to make progress in operational execution and in refining its business. Its orders rose substantially in the quarter and the company continues to plan for this business to achieve operating profitability by year-end 1997.
Unisys, based in Blue Bell, Pa., said its cash balance fell by about $340 million to about $700 million in the quarter.
